defects.cause: Every A* waypoint including the terminal one is voxelCoordToWorld(cell.support) — a snapped CELL CENTRE — and nextNavigationStep never consumes the last one, so it stays the steering target. steerFreeToward releases all four controls within tangent radius 0.2 of that centre, while walkToward only arrives on the distance to the goal the caller asked for. Chapter 13 aims CG_RAIL_CORNER_OVERSHOOT 0.6 THROUGH each route corner and stops at CG_RAIL_ROUTE_ARRIVE 0.35. With VOXEL_SCALE 2 the goal (-26,51.05,14.6) quantizes into the SAME cell as vertex 1 (-26,51.05,14), so the closest the body can come while steering is live is 0.6-0.2 = 0.4 > 0.35. The arrival predicate is analytically unsatisfiable, not merely unlucky.
defects.classification: snapped safe-cell navigation, NOT an obstacle, water, hole, rise/drop, cross-face edge or unreachable goal. Route reason is dry-surface-path with requestedGoalWasWet false and waterCrossing null; the verifier's ordinary-input discriminator moved the real body freely and supported stayed true with holdReason null.
defects.stillTimeExplanation: primitives.ts stuck watchdog accumulates stillTime only `if (pushing && horizontalDelta < 0.06)`, where pushing is forward||backward||left||right. In the dead zone the navigator issues NO control, so pushing is false and stillTime resets to 0 every frame beside a bit-identical body. The watchdog is not measuring the wrong body; it is correctly disarmed. No timeout teleport, nudge or rescue escalation was enabled by this repair.
defects.fix: terminalExactGoalHandoff + applyTerminalExactGoal in primitives.ts. At the terminal waypoint only, when the planner resolved the goal's OWN cell (dry-surface-path or already-at-resolved-goal, not wet, not substituted), the goal is same-face, the leg is not a water/jetpack leg, the goal falls inside the terminal cell's tangential footprint, and every further column the capsule actually overlaps is certified by the SAME planner at the SAME surface height — the aim moves tangentially onto the exact goal, at the height the planner cleared. The body then walks the remainder under ordinary directional input.
whatWasNotDone: steering dead zone 0.2 unchanged in value (named as NAVIGATION_STEER_DEAD_ZONE only so the arithmetic is testable)

defects.sharedWalkerSafetyArgument: Before the repair a body stopped within 0.2 of the snapped CENTRE, so arrival required stop >= 0.2 + |goal - centre|. After it, the body stops within 0.2 of the GOAL, so arrival requires only stop >= 0.2. The second condition is implied by the first for every offset, so no goal that used to be reached can stop being reached. The smallest stop radius anywhere in the shipped rails is 0.3 > 0.2. Terrain, obstacle, hazard, water and cross-face protection are untouched because the handoff never leaves a cell the planner certified and is refused outright on cross-face, water and substituted goals.

defects.cause: Two coupled defects. (A) commonGroundSnapshot returned a cached live snapshot for the actor BEFORE consulting the staged payload, so an empty placeholder minted during boot permanently shadowed the earned bytes staged a moment later by the world-keyed restore effect. (B) saveWorld writes a whole new WorldSave record, and its commonGround field was serializeCommonGroundForWorld(worldId) ?? undefined — so a placeholder overwrote the earned blob with emptiness, and a null would have deleted it outright.
defects.orderingIsolation: The write is NOT attributed to clicking Continue. The reproduction steps landing-menu boot, the placeholder-minting READ, the world switch to the sibling, and the world-change autosave separately, and names the read as the frame that creates the placeholder. The storage snapshot alone could not have identified this.
defects.fix: (1) serializeCommonGroundForWorld returns null for a snapshot that cannot speak for its world; (2) saveWorld carries the previously persisted commonGround forward instead of dropping or replacing it; (3) commonGroundSnapshot lets a staged payload take over an empty placeholder, never real progress; (4) a world is 'settled' only when its restore found NOTHING (absent/legacy) or when a payload actually VALIDATED — a completed read of a present payload settles nothing; (5) clearCommonGroundForWorld now also removes the stored chapter field so carry-forward cannot resurrect it.
defects.resumePointClassification: PC-CONTINUE-RESUME-POINT is a FIXTURE PREDECESSOR GAP, not a generalized wrong-world-selection bug. The deep link seeded story:ch13-fault-reviewed and story:ch13-return-chosen but never story:ch13-origin-landed, and storyState.storyEntryPoint resolves exactly that milestone set to ch13-return. Proved in both directions by test: without origin-landed the entry is ch13-return; with it, ch13-survey, and the same saved bytes resume the drawing.

reviewItems.resolution: certifyColumn now returns the planner's RESOLVED SURFACE rather than a boolean, and terminalExactGoalHandoff compares that height against the terminal waypoint along the up axis, refusing beyond half a cell with 'footprint-height-mismatch'. Dryness alone is not safety: a wall top and a pit floor are both dry. Proved with in-cube stepped terrain (plateau lowered to grid y 23 so a rise has real room), raised and lowered variants both refused, flat control still allowed.

A test drives the actual autopilotTick -> ch13 rail -> walkToward -> nextNavigationStep -> steerFreeToward wiring in movie mode with the body at the captured frozen pose, observing only the shipped getAutopilotControls(). It uses solely exports present on BOTH byte sets, so tmp/runtime-seam-counterfactual.py runs the same spec against pre-repair source: repaired 1 passed, pre-repair 'expected 0 to be greater than 0' — the shipped autopilot asked for no movement on any of 30 frames. Removing the runtime handoff fails behaviourally, as required.

The decision is cached per (plan, EXACT goal) via exactGoalHandoffFor, because the route cache tolerates a goal drifting up to one unit before replanning. The probes re-run only when the target actually moves; no full A* is forced. A focused same-plan test shows two targets under one unchanged plan, less than one unit apart, getting two different lawful answers (handoff vs footprint-not-certified).

The first 'entered' candidate was withdrawn: it made beat entry mean ownership, which would have made the very placeholder authoritative and reinstated the bug. Ownership is now driven only by persistence. Tests cover beat entry BEFORE staging (earned bytes survive an autosave in that window, then hydrate), a completed restore that finds nothing (emptiness becomes saveable), and a legitimately new action after a bare entry (never dropped).

clearCommonGroundForWorld clears the live/pending maps AND deletes the stored chapter field only, leaving structures, campfires, habitat and every other world alone. Tested that clear -> save -> reload does not resurrect the payload.

A completed read of a PRESENT payload no longer settles the world. isPristineCommonGround returns true while bytes are still pending, so an autosave landing between staging and hydration cannot let the placeholder answer. Test: enter -> placeholder -> restore -> IMMEDIATE saveWorld -> next tick; the earned drawing survives and then hydrates.

The foreign-actor test now rewrites the ACTUAL stored record and goes through restoreCommonGroundForWorld. A rejected payload deliberately does NOT settle the world, so this actor's empty state can never overwrite it; the bytes are retained across repeated autosaves. Documented consequence: a world holding another actor's payload stays unsettled and will not have local empty chapter state written over it.
getCommonGroundProbeSnapshot still reads the detached lastPublishedPlan; my runtime-seam test consumes it read-only AFTER ordinary ticks and adds no planner execution on inspection.

reproductionHonesty.initialGroundFrameCorrection: The first version of the navigation tests placed the body in the GROUNDED pose frame (y 50.989). The navigator reads getPlayerWorldPosition(), which is the capsule CENTRE (y 52.789, waypoint plane 52.85); in the wrong frame the cursor-consumption rise bound made a route leg look un-climbed and two cases failed for the wrong reason. Corrected to the centre frame, matching the capture, before any conclusion was drawn.
reproductionHonesty.integratorLimitation: The closed-loop walk tests advance the body with a small integrator that moves ONLY along the direction the shipped steering asked for, only while a control is held, at fixed speed. It can never teleport to or overshoot onto a requested point. The runtime-seam test needs no integrator at all: it observes the shipped controls directly.
